title: refactor(types,components,sdui-parser): retire the `body` child-list dialect — `children` is the one spelling (objectui#6771)
body:
Fixes #6771

> ## ⚠️ CORRECTION BLOCK — what this body gets wrong at head `b37fefa017cb7ff09456fc5de19ae45d93ebfc18`
>
> Re-stamped by the `domain:ui` seat at 2026-09-19T00:18Z, replacing the block written at 2026-09-18T19:49Z for head `25e0130eb…`. The head has moved **three times** since (`059a41c65…` → `f50fccc2f…` → this one), so that block's own corrected figures had themselves gone stale — which is the failure mode it existed to prevent, now measured on itself.
>
> ⛔ **This block is NOT claimed to be exhaustive.** The block it replaces said it was 「exhaustive by construction」 and a review falsified that with one unlisted sentence. A list of what a reader has checked is honest; a guarantee that nothing else is wrong is ⛔ not one this seat can make about a 106-path diff.
>
> **Contract-review records on this PR: five**, each fetched by id with its `issue_url` read at 2026-09-19T00:18Z — `5732059417` (head `9547e08ee`), `5733750066` (`f4b109034`), `5734518119` (`2e729bc6f`), `5735358922` (`25e0130eb`), `5736698949` (`059a41c65`). All five are **FAIL**. ⚠️ The fifth's **verdict is VOIDED** — `5736705386` records why: the reviewer ran below `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` because the seat spawned it without passing the tier. ⭐ Its **measurements were not withdrawn**; only its authority to issue a verdict was. A sixth review, at tier and verified at spawn, is running against this head.

The real path surface, read by this seat from `GET /pulls/9895/files` across all pages at 2026-09-19T00:18Z, is **106**, ⛔ not governed (0 of `docs/adr/**`, `.claude/**`, `skills/**`, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`), with a present-path control firing and a fabricated-path control reading absent.
> - 「159 nodes carrying `body` … before, 38 after」 — bound to an earlier head. `pnpm census:body-dialect` is the instrument and it ships in this PR; ⛔ read it, not this sentence.
> - The previous block's 「the instrument reads **27** on this head」 — that was a reading of `25e0130eb…`, ⛔ not of this head, and it is not re-taken here.
> - 「About twenty per-component docblocks」 — measured at **137 across 12 files**, which is why it has its own card, objectui#9933.

> ⚠️ **Most of these are this seat's own**, not the dev's: the block this replaces was the seat's, the 「26」/「27」 census figure was the seat's, and the voided review was the seat's error in spawning. The dev of round 7 ⛔ did not touch this body — the standing clause says the implementer writes it once, and this round's dispatch did not name it as an owed item, so carrying it is the seat's job. ⚠️ Which of the two rules governs when a dispatch *does* name it is with the maintainer as objectui#9976.
>
> **Not corrected here, and named so it is not lost:** the shipped changeset says the `page:card` retirement 「is objectui's」 without naming **objectui#9961**, the card this seat filed for it after this head was cut. ⛔ Not a falsified sentence — an uncited carrier, and the seat's call whether the CHANGELOG paragraph should carry it.

Clause-②: yes

⭐ **Resolved by the seat on 2026-09-18, exactly the way the note below asks:** the declaration of record is this card's claim comment, which re-declares `yes`, and `needs:contract-review` is hung on both carriers. The `no` that stood on this line was the **dispatch's** score — ⛔ the note below is unchanged and was right to refuse to resolve it silently.

⚠️ **The ruling this executes says otherwise for one of its five steps, and I am not choosing between them silently.** The dispatch scored this card `no` on the ground that it NARROWS an accepted authoring set. The 2026-09-01 ruling scores its own **step 3** — retiring `body` from the published type — as **`Clause-② yes at dispatch`**, and triage's 2026-09-17 answer bound the `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` quota to that step alone. Today's release record (comment `5730313581`) argued only the producer-side condition, which binds steps 2 / 4 / 5. ⇒ **step 3's recorded condition was not addressed by the release that unblocked this card**, and whether it is live today is a seat reading, not mine. I have drafted the whole ruling; the `needs:contract-review` label is the seat's to attach and I have neither attached nor waited for it.

---

## What this is

The maintainer ruling of 2026-09-01 (「同意。」, option B) retires the `body` child-list dialect: one concept, one spelling, and the spelling is `children`. Step 1 (the liveness census) landed as #7184. **This is steps 2 through 5.**

`BaseSchema` declared two spellings and left the choice per component. Twelve registrations read `body` and nothing else, so it was their only door; the wider set read `children || body` and took either. The authoring tier only ever knew `children` — so an author writing the one spelling that resolved got `unknown-prop`, the same warning a typo draws, on the tier built for AI authors where the diagnostic **is** the contract.

## The five steps, and where each one landed

| step | state |
|---|---|
| 1 — census | landed earlier (#7184); re-run here as the verification instrument |
| 2 — converge the `body`-only registrations; fallback readers drop the arm in the same change | this PR |
| 3 — retire `body` from the published type | this PR ⚠️ see the Clause-② note above |
| 4 — the tier teaches `children` only | this PR |
| 5 — corpus and teaching migrate in the same commit | this PR |

**Step 2.** `alert`, `badge`, `tooltip` and the ten `sidebar-*` reads converge on `children`. Every `children || body` fallback drops its `body` arm: `basic/div.tsx`, `layout/card.tsx`, `layout/semantic.tsx`, `layout/aspect-ratio.tsx`, `form/button.tsx` (named in the ruling's own cross-card boundary paragraph), `layout/page.tsx`'s three reads, `@object-ui/core`'s recursive `validateSchema`, the two container walkers that enumerated child channels, and both VS Code extension readers — whose own comments deferred the arm to this card by number.

**Step 3.** `BaseSchema.body` is `never` on the TypeScript face and an alias refusal naming `children` on the Zod mirror, as are the four per-component redeclarations. **Refused by name, not deleted** — `BaseSchema` carries `[key: string]: any` and the mirror ends `.passthrough()`, so a deleted member is accepted silently and rendered by nothing, which is the exact silence this retirement ends.

**Step 4.** A new `sdui-parser/src/body-dialect.ts` answers an authored `body` with the replacement NAMED, and it REPLACES the diagnostic the prop walk would emit rather than stacking on it — the shape `checkKanbanQuickAdd` next door is written against. A `body` child list under a non-container draws the same containment code the `children` spelling draws, which is the ruling's own sentence.

**Step 5.** 114 authored nodes moved across the docs site, the schema catalog, five package READMEs and the extension's snippets / JSON schema / syntax map / hovers / completions, plus the prose that taught the key.

## ⚠️ A contrary fact, measured while implementing step 2 — pinned, not worked around

Converging the twelve gives them a `children` read, so #6808's runtime predicate calls them containers. #6804's ruling anticipated this and wrote the answer in advance, verbatim: a census-pin exception **with its ground**, ⛔ not `isContainer`. That is what landed — ten reasoned entries in `container-declaration-baseline.json`'s `excluded`, and its exact-equality pin moved with them.

**But the exception is no longer free, and the cost is this card's own defect one key over:**

| | renders | draws `not-a-container` |
|---|---|---|
| before | `body` | `children` |
| after | `children` | `children` |

`validateTree`'s containment branch reads `node.children?.length`, so the false warning that used to sit on a key these registrations did not read now sits on the only key they do. Per the standing clause I executed the ruling literally, made no promote and no revert in this PR, and **inverted the pin into a refusal** that states the cost (`container-declaration-ratchet.test.tsx`, the converged-readers block).

⇒ **The question for whoever reads this:** #6804's ground — `children` here is a *label / content fallback*, not layout containment — transfers cleanly to `badge`, `alert`, `button` and `tooltip`. It does not obviously transfer to the `sidebar-*` family, whose child lists ARE layout containment and which are NOT in the public tier, so the react-page cost that justified `button`'s exclusion does not apply to them either. That ruling was made before the convergence existed. ⛔ Not decided here.

## Two readers deliberately left alone, each with its ground

- **`page:card`** still reads `schema?.body ?? schema?.children`. That key is `PageCardProps.body` under a **different** retirement (objectstack#5775, ADR-0087 D2), and its own comment records a sequencing precondition — the load-time `body` to `children` conversion — that deleting the read before would blank stored documents silently.
- **`items[]`-level `body`** on `list` (and the same shape on `tabs` items and `dashboard` widgets) is objectui#9590's card, fenced off this one. ⛔ Untouched, in either direction.

## Verification

- `pnpm census:body-dialect`, the instrument step 1 committed for exactly this re-reading: **159 nodes carrying `body` on the retirement's keys before, 38 after** — and all 38 are test fixtures, the scanner's own planted fixtures, or two pre-existing changesets this branch does not own.
- `packages/types` + `packages/sdui-parser`: **221 files, 5009 tests, all passing.**
- `packages/components`: **282 files, 2743 tests, all passing.**
- Changeset gates green: presence (1 declared), no-major, no-overwrite. Control bytes green. Governed-surface guard: NOT GOVERNED, 81 paths checked.

## Files outside the dispatched surface, declared rather than widened silently

The dispatch named `packages/components/src/renderers/`, `packages/sdui-parser/src/` and `packages/types/src/base.ts`. The ruling's steps 2, 3 and 5 reach further and each of these is named for that reason: the rest of `packages/types/src` (the four redeclarations, their mirrors, the pins that move with them), `packages/core/src/validation/schema-validator.ts` (a generic `children || body` reader), `packages/vscode-extension/**` (two readers that deferred to this card, plus the teaching surfaces), `scripts/container-declaration-baseline.json` (#6804's ordered exception), `content/docs/**`, `examples/schema-catalog/**` and five READMEs (step 5).

## Acceptance notes

Noted while measuring, ⛔ not filed and ⛔ not repaired here:

- `dashboard` widgets author a per-widget `body` (`content/docs/api/schema-reference.md`, `plugin-dashboard/README.md`'s vocabulary note) that no renderer reads — same item-level family as objectui#9590.
- About twenty per-component `body?: never` docblocks still justify themselves with "`body` is inherited-and-optional from `BaseSchema`, whose own docblock admits …". The refusals are correct and stay word-for-word; only that one premise sentence is now stale.
- Two pre-existing changesets carry `body` migration recipes that will teach the retired spelling when they reach a CHANGELOG. Not edited — they belong to other cards and `check-changeset-overwrite` reports a branch that modifies them.
